title: Food Tours in Kuala Lumpur
heroDescription: Kuala Lumpur is where Malay, Chinese, and Indian culinary traditions meet. Our three KL tours each explore a different side of the city: Flavours of Malaysia visits Chow Kit's wet market (4 hours, RM 289), KL Street Food walks through Chinatown's Petaling Street (3.5 hours, RM 285), and Secrets of KL is an evening tour through Chinatown's hidden speakeasies (4 hours, RM 359). All start at central meeting points — Hilton Garden Inn or Pasar Seni LRT.
content:
## The KL Tour Experience

Each tour covers about 2 km of easy walking. Groups are capped at 9 people so you can actually talk to vendors and ask questions. Every tour includes 8-10 tastings plus a full meal.

## Our KL Guide: Pauline

Pauline grew up shopping for groceries with her mum at the very markets we visit — Petaling Street and Chow Kit. She knows the vendors by face, knows which stalls have been there since she was a child, and can tell you how the neighbourhoods have changed over the years. She's also been eating in Pudu since she was young, and we're developing a new tour in that area.

## What You'll Taste

On our KL tours, you'll try Nasi Lemak (coconut rice with sambal, anchovies and egg), Roti Canai (flaky flatbread with dhal curry), Satay (grilled meat skewers with peanut sauce), Cendol (shaved ice with coconut milk and palm sugar), Curry Laksa (spicy coconut noodle soup), and Char Kway Teow (stir-fried flat rice noodles).

## Dietary Accommodation

All KL tours accommodate vegetarian, vegan, halal, and gluten-free diets. Just let us know when booking — we brief the stalls before you arrive.

title: Food Tours in Penang
heroDescription: Penang is widely considered the food capital of Malaysia. George Town's UNESCO World Heritage core is lined with hawker stalls that have been perfecting their recipes for generations. Our two Penang tours cover different sides of the island's food scene: Eat Drink George Town is an evening tour with speakeasy cocktails and 10+ tastings (4 hours, RM 359), and Penang Street Food is a daytime exploration starting on Penang Road (3.5 hours, RM 285). Both start at Masjid Kapitan Keling.
content:
## Penang's Food Heritage

Penang's food is shaped by its Peranakan (Straits Chinese) heritage. Char kway teow, asam laksa, and cendol were all perfected here. The island's hawker culture runs deep — many stalls have been in the same family for two or three generations.

## Our Penang Guides

Our Penang team includes Wei Shen, Gary, Ronald, and others who grew up eating in the back lanes of George Town. They know the best stalls for Penang's famous asam laksa, the family behind the legendary char kway teow, and where to find the perfect cendol. Many of our guests — like Sue, Holden, and Jim — mention our guides by name in their reviews.

## What You'll Taste

Expect char kway teow (stir-fried rice noodles with prawns), asam laksa (sour fish noodle soup), cendol (shaved ice dessert), satay, roti canai, and Penang's famous Hokkien mee. On the evening tour, you'll also visit a hidden speakeasy for a signature cocktail. Each stop includes the story behind the dish and why Penang's version is unique.

## Dietary Accommodation

All Penang tours accommodate vegetarian, vegan, halal, and gluten-free diets. We brief the stalls before you arrive.

title: Food Tours in Melaka
heroDescription: Melaka is where Malaysia's food story began. 600 years of Portuguese, Dutch, British, Chinese, and Malay influence have created a cuisine you won't find anywhere else. Jonker Street comes alive at night with food stalls, and the city's Nyonya restaurants serve dishes passed down through generations.
content:
## Melaka's Unique Cuisine

Melaka is the birthplace of Peranakan (Nyonya) cuisine — a beautiful fusion of Chinese ingredients with Malay spices and cooking methods. Dishes like ayam buah keluak, nyonya laksa, and cendol originate here. Portuguese-Eurasian cuisine, with its unique blends, is another Melaka speciality.

title: Food Tours in Ipoh
heroDescription: Ipoh is a hidden gem of Malaysian food. This former tin-mining town has a laid-back charm and a food scene to match. Famous for its white coffee, bean sprout chicken, and old-town kopitiams (coffee shops), Ipoh rewards those who take the time to explore.
content:
## Ipoh's Food Specialities

Ipoh is famous for several dishes you won't find done better anywhere else. The bean sprout chicken — poached chicken served with crunchy local bean sprouts — is legendary. Ipoh white coffee, a slightly caramelised coffee drink, originated here. The town's Hakka influences add another dimension to its food.

title: Food Tours in Klang
heroDescription: Klang is the birthplace of bak kut teh — the aromatic pork rib soup that has become a Malaysian staple. This port town has a rich food heritage shaped by its Hokkien Chinese community and its history as a trading hub. Klang's food is bold, earthy, and deeply satisfying.
content:
## Klang's Culinary Claims to Fame

Bak kut teh (pork rib soup) was invented in Klang, and the town still has some of the best versions in Malaysia. Klang's Hokkien mee — thick noodles in dark soy sauce — is another local speciality. The town's proximity to the coast means fresh seafood features prominently in its cuisine.
